items.briefing:
Australia's corporate watchdog ASIC has warned that scammers are increasingly using AI to build convincing deepfake investment scam networks targeting Australians — if an investment opportunity looks or sounds too polished, treat it with suspicion. Separately, a China-linked hacker has demonstrated advanced AI capabilities in attacks across the Asia-Pacific region, putting Australian organisations on alert. A critical zero-click vulnerability in GitLab has also been disclosed, meaning organisations using GitLab should apply patches promptly without waiting for user interaction to trigger the flaw.

OpenAI has introduced a teen-specific version of ChatGPT with safety features now available in Australia — worth noting for any staff with young family members using the platform. **Practical tip:** If you receive an unsolicited investment offer online — especially one featuring video testimonials — verify the person's identity independently before engaging, as deepfake technology can make fake spokespeople appear completely real

featured.title: PCI council marks 20 years with AI focus in Kuala Lumpur
featured.summary: Banks and merchants face fresh fraud risks as the council's Kuala Lumpur meeting weighs how AI is changing payment security.
